# Make Mobile Web Apps Feel Installed, Not Embedded

> Eliminate sticky touch hover states, viewport URL-bar clipping, gray tap flashes, and accidental text selection on mobile web interfaces.

- Section: Physical Ergonomics
- URL: http://127.0.0.1:3000/mobile-native-physics
- Published: 2026-04-12
- Source: https://github.com/first-principles-ui/first-principles-ui/blob/main/content/physical-ergonomics/mobile-native-physics.mdx

> **Interactive demo: Mobile Native Physics.** Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/mobile-native-physics to try it.

Unconditional `:hover` styles stay stuck after tapping on mobile screens, while raw `100vh` clips beneath browser chrome. Gate hover effects behind `@media (hover: hover)` and use dynamic viewport units (`100dvh`) with `touch-action: manipulation`.

Mobile web applications often feel clunky and amateurish not because of JavaScript execution speed, but because of neglected mobile physics: sticky `:hover` styles, viewport clipping behind dynamic browser address bars, and default tap flash artifacts.

## Capability-Gated Hover States

Touchscreens do not have a persistent hover cursor. When an author writes an unconditional `:hover` rule, mobile browsers simulate hover on tap—and leave the element permanently stuck in its hover style until the user taps somewhere else.

`LAW_28_MOBILE_CAPABILITY_GATE` requires isolating hover treatments to devices that genuinely possess precision pointers and hover hardware:

```css
/* Right: Only devices with genuine hover hardware */
@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) {
  .interactive-card:hover {
    background-color: var(--color-muted);
    border-color: var(--color-border-active);
  }
}
```

## Dynamic Viewport Units (`100dvh` vs. `100vh`)

On mobile browsers like Safari and Chrome for iOS/Android, the browser address bar dynamically expands and retracts during scrolling. Classic `100vh` calculates viewport height assuming the address bar is retracted—causing bottom action buttons and floating drawers to be clipped underneath the visible browser chrome.

Modern web standards introduce dynamic viewport units:
- `100dvh`: Dynamically adjusts as the address bar retracts or appears.
- `100svh`: The smallest possible viewport height (when address bar is fully expanded).
- `100lvh`: The largest possible viewport height (when address bar is fully retracted).

## Touch Action & Selection Discipline

Interactive controls (buttons, chips, segmented tabs, icons) must never trigger browser text selection or double-tap zoom delays:

```css
.touch-control {
  user-select: none;
  -webkit-user-select: none;
  -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
  touch-action: manipulation;
}
```

## Resources

- [MDN: CSS @media (hover)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/hover): Testing whether the user's primary input mechanism can hover over elements.

# Keep Animations on the GPU & Choose the Right Easing

> Enforce physical spring easing curves, strict GPU compositor property isolation (transform and opacity), and a 400ms Doherty response latency ceiling.

- Section: Physical Ergonomics
- URL: http://127.0.0.1:3000/motion-choreography
- Published: 2026-11-09
- Source: https://github.com/first-principles-ui/first-principles-ui/blob/main/content/physical-ergonomics/motion-choreography.mdx

> **Interactive demo: Motion Choreography Rule.** Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/motion-choreography to try it.

Animating `width` or `padding` forces synchronous CPU layout reflow, dropping frames to stuttery lag. Restrict animations to GPU-composited `transform` and `opacity` with critically damped springs (`zeta >= 0.85`) settling under 350ms.

## Spring Easings & Press States

> **Interactive demo: Demo Tab Group.** Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/motion-choreography to try it.
    <EasingCurveDemo />
    <StrongEasingDemo />
  </DemoTab>
  <DemoTab label="Tactile Press">
    <ButtonPressDemo />
    <PressAmountDemo />
  </DemoTab>
</DemoTabGroup>

Sluggish transitions and mechanical linear animations make digital interfaces feel cheap and unresponsive. Worse, using `transition: all` forces the browser engine to recalculate geometric layout on every animation frame, causing dropped frames and sluggish mobile scrolling.

1. **Spring Deceleration Curves:** Mechanical `linear` transitions move at constant speed and stop abruptly, violating physical inertia. Physical objects decelerate smoothly into place. Easing curves like `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` mimic critically damped springs, providing instant feedback with a natural settle.
2. **Compositor Property Isolation:** The browser rendering pipeline splits work into Layout, Paint, and Composite. Animating `width`, `height`, or `margin` forces continuous re-layout across the DOM tree. Modern interfaces must animate only GPU-accelerated compositor properties: `transform`, `opacity`, and color tokens.
3. **Doherty Response Budget:** The Doherty threshold establishes that human interaction feels instantaneous when system feedback completes within 400ms. Choreographed animations where total duration plus delay exceeds 400ms introduce perceived drag.

## Remediation

Isolate transitions to specific compositor tokens and specify high-performance spring easing:

```css
/* Good: GPU-accelerated spring transition */
.btn-action {
  transition-property: transform, opacity, background-color, border-color;
  transition-duration: 200ms;
  transition-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1);
}

.btn-action:hover {
  transform: translateY(-1px);
}
```

<details className="my-8 rounded-2xl border border-border/70 bg-muted/15 p-4 sm:p-5">
  <summary className="cursor-pointer text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground flex items-center justify-between">
    <span>Under the Hood: Mathematical Formula &amp; Verifier Source</span>
    <span className="rounded-full bg-muted px-2 py-0.5 text-[10px] font-mono">Optional Deep Dive</span>
  </summary>
  <div className="mt-4 space-y-4 text-xs text-muted-foreground">
The engine inspects computed transition properties across all visible interactive elements:

> **Transition Easing:** `timing-function != linear` (spring / cubic-bezier curve)  
> **Compositor Isolation:** `property != all` (isolated to transform, opacity, color tokens)  
> **Choreography Budget:** `duration + delay <= 400ms` (Doherty threshold)

<details className="my-6 rounded-xl border border-border/60 bg-muted/20 p-4">
  <summary className="cursor-pointer text-xs font-mono font-medium text-muted-foreground">
    View Deterministic Playwright Verifier Source (check-ui-math.mjs)
  </summary>

```typescript
// Evaluated by src/rules/motion-choreography.mjs
for (const el of allVisible) {
  const cs = getComputedStyle(el);

  // 1. Flag linear easing
  if (cs.transitionTimingFunction === "linear" && cs.transitionDuration !== "0s") {
    ctx.report("LAW_15_LINEAR_EASING", {
      property: "transition-timing-function",
      computed: "linear",
      threshold: "cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)",
    });
  }

  // 2. Layout thrash guard
  if (cs.transitionDuration !== "0s" && cs.transitionProperty === "all") {
    ctx.report("LAW_15_LAYOUT_THRASH_ANIMATION", {
      property: "transition-property",
      computed: "all",
      threshold: "transform, opacity, color, background-color, border-color",
    });
  }
}
```

</details>
  </div>
</details>

- [Doherty Threshold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doherty_threshold): Human-computer interaction latency ceiling for maintaining user engagement.
- [Web Animations & Compositor Pipeline](https://web.dev/articles/animations-guide): Hardware-accelerated transitions via GPU transform and opacity layers.

# Morph States & Shared Layouts Without Distortion

> Ensure continuous visual flow across container changes, shared element transitions, optical icon morphs, and asymmetric exit reflows without glyph stretching or GPU paint thrashing.

- Section: Physical Ergonomics
- URL: http://127.0.0.1:3000/fluid-continuity
- Published: 2026-11-10
- Source: https://github.com/first-principles-ui/first-principles-ui/blob/main/content/physical-ergonomics/fluid-continuity.mdx

> **Interactive demo: Fluid Continuity Rule.** Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/fluid-continuity to try it.

Unconstrained layout morphs warp font glyph aspect ratios during container expansion, while sluggish dismissals trap user attention. Enforce uniform scale projection (`|scaleX - scaleY| <= 0.04`) and make exit animations 2x faster than entrances.

## Continuous Fluid Interactions & State Morphing

> **Interactive demo: Demo Tab Group.** Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/fluid-continuity to try it.
    <SharedLayoutDetailDemo />
  </DemoTab>
  <DemoTab label="2. Icon Morph" badge="sigma <= 4px">
    <IconMorphDemo />
    <IconMorphTuningDemo />
    <RotationMorphDemo />
    <HamburgerMorphDemo />
  </DemoTab>
  <DemoTab label="3. Asymmetric Exit" badge="0.5x Enter">
    <ExitAnimationsDemo />
    <ExitListDemo />
  </DemoTab>
  <DemoTab label="4. Clip-Path Reveal" badge="GPU">
    <ClipPathRevealDemo />
    <ClipPathTabsDemo />
    <ClipPathHoldDemo />
    <ClipPathCompareDemo />
  </DemoTab>
</DemoTabGroup>

1. **Aspect-Ratio Scale Invariance:** When expanding a small card (`W1/H1`) into a large details view (`W2/H2`), container scale factors diverge (`scaleX != scaleY`). Applying this matrix transform directly to text causes visible distortion. Text children must decouple via `layout="position"` to maintain an isotropic 1:1 scale (`|scaleX - scaleY| <= 0.04`).
2. **Optical Blur Bridging vs. Geometric Rotation:** When two icons share topological symmetry (such as `+` and `×`, or chevrons), state changes should execute via pure geometric rotation (`transform: rotate(45deg)`) with zero GPU rasterization cost. For topologically distinct icons (such as Copy and Check), an optical blur bridge (`blur(4px)` + critically damped spring `zeta = 1.0`) provides perceptual continuity without raster stalls.
3. **Asymmetric Exit Velocity:** When users dismiss a surface (modal, sheet, toast, or list row), their cognitive task is complete. Lingering exits waste attention. Systems must enforce an asymmetric exit ratio:
   `T_exit = round(0.5 * T_enter) <= 200ms`
4. **Compositor Clip-Path Continuity:** Sliding segmented indicators and progress indicators must utilize compositor-accelerated `clip-path: inset()` rather than DOM restructuring to achieve seamless inverted-color reveals.

## Remediation

Protect child typography inside morphing containers and enforce asymmetric exit timings:

```tsx
/* Good: Text protected with layout="position", asymmetric exit duration */
<motion.div layout layoutId="card-container" className="card">
  <motion.h3 layout="position" className="text-lg font-bold">
    Live Cluster Metrics
  </motion.h3>
  <AnimatePresence>
    {isOpen && (
      <motion.div
        initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
        animate={{ opacity: 1, transition: { duration: 0.24 } }}
        exit={{ opacity: 0, transition: { duration: 0.12 } }}
      >
        <p>Expanded telemetric details</p>
      </motion.div>
    )}
  </AnimatePresence>
</motion.div>
```

<details className="my-8 rounded-2xl border border-border/70 bg-muted/15 p-4 sm:p-5">
  <summary className="cursor-pointer text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground flex items-center justify-between">
    <span>Under the Hood: Mathematical Formula &amp; Verifier Source</span>
    <span className="rounded-full bg-muted px-2 py-0.5 text-[10px] font-mono">Optional Deep Dive</span>
  </summary>
  <div className="mt-4 space-y-4 text-xs text-muted-foreground">
The engine inspects computed transforms, active filters, and exit transition properties:

> **Text Glyph Aspect Invariance:** `|scaleX - scaleY| <= 0.04` on text children  
> **Filter Paint Budget:** `blur(r) <= 12px` on containers `<= 6400px²` (max 3 sibling rows)  
> **Asymmetric Exit Ceiling:** `T_exit <= 200ms` on closing / exiting states

<details className="my-6 rounded-xl border border-border/60 bg-muted/20 p-4">
  <summary className="cursor-pointer text-xs font-mono font-medium text-muted-foreground">
    View Deterministic Playwright Verifier Source (check-ui-math.mjs)
  </summary>

```typescript
// Evaluated by src/rules/flip-continuity.mjs
const cs = getComputedStyle(el);

// 1. Non-uniform text scale guard
if (scaleDiff > 0.04) {
  ctx.report("LAW_31_FLIP_CONTINUITY_HYGIENE", {
    property: "transform",
    computed: `scaleX=${scaleX.toFixed(2)}, scaleY=${scaleY.toFixed(2)}`,
    threshold: "|scaleX - scaleY| <= 0.04",
    ast_instruction: 'Apply layout="position" to child text elements.',
  });
}

// 2. Filter paint budget
if (blurRadius > 12 && boxArea > 6400) {
  ctx.report("LAW_31_FLIP_CONTINUITY_HYGIENE", {
    property: "filter",
    computed: `blur(${blurRadius}px) on ${boxArea}px²`,
    threshold: "blur(r <= 12px) on area <= 6400px²",
  });
}

// 3. Asymmetric exit duration
if (isExiting && durSeconds > 0.2) {
  ctx.report("LAW_31_FLIP_CONTINUITY_HYGIENE", {
    property: "transition-duration",
    computed: `${Math.round(durSeconds * 1000)}ms`,
    threshold: "<= 200ms",
  });
}
```

# Delete Motion on High-Frequency & Keyboard Actions

> Eliminate animation fatigue by scaling duration inversely with interaction frequency: instant keyboard shortcuts, warm tooltip handoffs, capped list staggers, and optimistic updates.

- Section: Physical Ergonomics
- URL: http://127.0.0.1:3000/interaction-frequency
- Published: 2026-04-12
- Source: https://github.com/first-principles-ui/first-principles-ui/blob/main/content/physical-ergonomics/interaction-frequency.mdx

> **Interactive demo: Novelty Budget.** Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/interaction-frequency to try it.

Everyday utility actions should never demand attention with flashy decorative animations. Spend novelty budgets exclusively on celebratory milestone events, keeping high-frequency repetitive tasks instant (`< 100ms`).

## Frequency Delays & Optimistic UI

> **Interactive demo: Demo Tab Group.** Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/interaction-frequency to try it.
    <HoverTooltipDemo />
  </DemoTab>
  <DemoTab label="Stagger Delays">
    <StaggerDemo />
    <StaggerCapDemo />
  </DemoTab>
  <DemoTab label="Perceived Speed">
    <LoadingFlashDemo />
    <OptimisticDemo />
  </DemoTab>
</DemoTabGroup>
Animation has a novelty half-life. A 400ms entrance that delights on day 1 becomes an infuriating tax by day 30 when repeated 200 times a day.

## The Frequency-Duration Inverse Law

`LAW_29_HIGH_FREQ_MOTION_TAX` states that animation duration must scale inversely with interaction frequency:

1. **High-Frequency Actions (`f >= 100 / day`):** Duration must be `0ms` (instantaneous).
2. **Keyboard-Triggered Actions:** When an action is invoked via a keyboard shortcut (e.g. `Cmd+K`, arrow keys, `Esc`), users operate in cognitive command mode. Motion duration must not exceed `100ms`.
3. **Staggered Entrances:** Cumulative stagger delay across any list or grid must be capped at `sum(delta_t) <= 300ms`.

## Warm Tooltip Handoffs

When a user hovers over the first icon in a toolbar, a brief delay (e.g. 300ms) prevents unwanted flashes. But once a tooltip is open, subsequent hovers across adjacent icons must open instantly with zero delay:

## Capping Stagger Delays

Staggering 20 list items at 50ms each forces the user to wait a full second before the final item appears. Caps prevent this latency:

## Perceived Performance & Optimistic UI

Loading spinners that flash for less than 150ms increase perceived latency compared to rendering nothing or applying optimistic updates:

# Make Gestures, Sheets & Popovers Interruptible

> Build physically grounded gesture sheets and popovers with 1:1 pointer tracking, velocity-seeded spring releases, critical damping, and interruptible state machines.

- Section: Physical Ergonomics
- URL: http://127.0.0.1:3000/spring-gesture-physics
- Published: 2026-04-12
- Source: https://github.com/first-principles-ui/first-principles-ui/blob/main/content/physical-ergonomics/spring-gesture-physics.mdx

> **Interactive demo: Interrupt Sheet.** Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/spring-gesture-physics to try it.

Animations that lock out touch input break direct physical manipulation and make apps feel unresponsive. Keep all gesture interactions interruptible with momentum-preserving velocity handoff (`v_exit = v_gesture`), letting users redirect in flight.

## Gesture Momentum & Direct Tracking

> **Interactive demo: Demo Tab Group.** Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/spring-gesture-physics to try it.
  </DemoTab>
  <DemoTab label="Input Locking Guard">
    <InterruptLockDemo />
  </DemoTab>
  <DemoTab label="Scale & Origin">
    <ScaleEntrancesDemo />
    <TransformOriginDemo />
  </DemoTab>
</DemoTabGroup>
When users touch a digital surface, they expect Newtonian physics: objects track fingers with zero latency, retain velocity upon release, and can be caught mid-flight without locking input.

## Two-Phase Direct Manipulation

`LAW_30_SPRING_INTERRUPTIBILITY` models interactive sheets and cards as two distinct physical phases:

1. **Phase 1: Direct Tracking (1:1 Drag):** The element tracks pointer translation directly with zero spring lag. Damping and stiffness do not apply during active drag.
2. **Phase 2: Velocity-Seeded Spring Release:** When released, the solver projects pointer velocity ($v_0$) into a second-order harmonic oscillator:
   `m * x'' + c * x' + k * x = 0`

Solving this differential equation with critical damping (`zeta = c / (2 * sqrt(m * k)) = 1.0`) ensures the element settles at its target boundary in minimum time without underdamped bouncing or sluggish overdamping.

## Never Lock User Input

Many web libraries disable click and pointer events (`pointer-events: none`) while an entrance or exit animation runs. This violates Apple HIG and First-Principles UI ergonomics:

## Scale Entrances & Transform Origins

Scale entrances should start close to their resting size (`s0 >= 0.95`) and expand directly from their trigger button:

## Resources

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Motion](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/motion): Designing realistic, fluid, and responsive spring animations.
